name: Figs
why_now: Mission figs peak in late July through August. The window is short — often just two or three weeks of genuinely perfect fruit. What you find now was picked ripe and won't be available like this again until next year.
how_to_choose: Deep purple to almost black — that's ripe, not overripe
Slightly soft when gently pressed, especially near the base
Sometimes splitting at the base — that's a good sign
A small bead of sweetness near the stem means it's ready
Avoid pale green or tan figs; they haven't ripened
buy_this_much: 1 pint for the week. Plan to eat most of them within two days of buying.
price_note: Figs are briefly abundant in August and reasonably priced at farmers markets. Grocery store figs are available but often picked underripe for transport — the farmers market version is worth the detour this month.

flavor_paths.name: Nearly nothing
flavor_paths.description: Halved and eaten as they are. Salt if you want it.

flavor_paths.name: Sweet
flavor_paths.description: Sliced on yogurt with a little honey. That's breakfast.

flavor_paths.name: Savory
flavor_paths.description: With prosciutto, burrata, and arugula. The weekend plate.

weekday_uses: Halved on Greek yogurt in the morning
Eaten as a snack, ripe, over the sink
weekend_use: The weekend plate: halved figs, torn burrata, prosciutto, arugula, olive oil, and flaky salt. Eat with bread.
storage: Counter for a day, two at most. Refrigerate only if necessary and use immediately after. Do not buy them expecting them to keep.
one_thing_to_learn: A fig ripens from the outside in, not the inside out. The color tells you something. Black-purple with a soft give near the base is ready. A hard, pale fig won't ripen meaningfully on the counter — it will soften but not sweeten the way a tree-ripened one does.
market_question: Which variety is this? Are these mission figs?
